title: Ruling 2025-03: Sales of Parking Permits Not Subject to Sales and Use Tax
text:
Date: October 1, 2025

Written by: Matthew Phillips, Assistant Attorney General

Approved by: William C. Shouldice, IV, Commissioner of Taxes

This is a formal ruling for [Taxpayers] regarding the Vermont Sales and Use Tax treatment of parking permits sold through third-party software. This ruling is based upon representations communicated in your emails dated [date] and [date].

Facts 

1. [Taxpayer] is a public corporation [deleted].

2. As part of its operations, [deleted] maintains parking lots and offers parking permits for sale to [customers].

3. [Taxpayer] intends to utilize a third-party vendor's software to process parking permit transactions and payments electronically. [Customers] will purchase the permit online and will receive a receipt of the transaction. Payments to [Taxpayer] will be made via a payment processor.

Discussion 

You asked whether [Taxpayer] 's sales of parking permits, as described above, are subject to Vermont Sales and Use Tax. These transactions are not subject to Vermont Sales and Use Tax.

Vermont Sales and Use Tax applies to retail sales made in Vermont. 32 V.S.A. §§ 9771, 9773. "Retail sale" includes any sale, lease, or rental for a consideration for any purpose other than for resale, sublease, or subrent. 32 V.S.A. § 9701(5), (4)(A); Vt. Reg. § 1.9701(5)-1.

Only certain types of retail sales are subject to Vermont Sales and Use Tax. The types of retail sales subject to Vermont Sales and Use Tax are listed in 32 V.S.A. § 9771. Vermont Sales and Use Tax most commonly applies to sales or leases of tangible personal property, not real

property. 32 V.S.A. § 9771(1); Vt. Reg. 1.9701(5)-1. Vermont Sales and Use Tax also applies to sales of certain services (e.g., admissions to places of entertainment; telecommunications services). 32 V.S.A. § 9771(4)&(5).

None of the categories listed in Section 9771 apply to the rental of parking spaces. Parking spaces are not tangible personal property for purposes of Vermont's Sales and Use Tax; nor is the rental of parking spaces a taxable service. It is more akin to the rental of real property,

which is not subject to the Sales and Use Tax. Therefore, the transactions described above are not subject to Vermont's Sales and Use Tax.

General Provisions 

Issuance of this ruling is conditioned upon the understanding that neither the taxpayer nor a related taxpayer is currently under audit or involved in an administrative appeal or litigation concerning the subject matters of the ruling. This ruling is issued solely to the taxpayer and is limited to the facts presented, as affected by current statutes and regulations.

Other taxpayers may refer to this ruling, when redacted to protect confidentiality, to see the Department's general approach, but the Department will not be bound by this ruling in the case of any other taxpayer or in the case of any change in the relevant statutes or regulations.

This ruling will be made public after deletion of the taxpayer's name and any information that may identify the taxpayer. A copy of this ruling showing the proposed deletions is attached, and you may request within 30 days that the Commissioner delete any further information that

might identify the taxpayer. The final discretion as to deletions rests with the Commissioner.

You have the right to appeal this ruling within 30 days. 3 VS.A.§§ 808,815.
